The direct callers of `OrderSetService.saveOrderSet` in the REST module are in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, the `/ws/rest/v1` module. I found them with one repo-wide grep (38 matches across 8 files, not truncated) and read the call sites. The service itself is in `openmrs-core`, but that is the changed code, not a consumer, so it is not listed.

1. **`OrderSetResource1_12.save`** (lines 57–72) is the main production path. It is the `save` override for the `/ws/rest/v1/order set` resource and returns `Context.getOrderSetService().saveOrderSet(orderSet)` at line 71. Any change in what `saveOrderSet` returns, validates, or persists changes the REST create and update response for order sets.
2. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.delete`** (lines 151–155) retires a member and then calls `saveOrderSet` on the parent (line 154). A change in retirement or save semantics affects member deletion.
3. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.save`** (lines 163–168) adds the member to its parent and calls `saveOrderSet(parent)` (line 166). This is the create and update path for `/ordersetmember` sub-resources.
4. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.purge`** (lines 171–175) removes the member from the parent and calls `saveOrderSet` (line 174). A change affects hard-delete behaviour.
5. **`OrderSetMemberController1_12Test`** (lines 79–88) is a test, not production code. It calls `saveOrderSet` at line 85 to set up data for the member listing test, so it may need updating if the behaviour changes.

Other classes in the module, such as `OrderSetResource1_12.getByUniqueId` and `getAll`, call the service but not `saveOrderSet`, so they are not affected by this change.
